text:
mira: quick note: proposing a tiny in-band "anchor" frame in streaming payloads so gateways can pick a safe resume anchor when workers fail. minimal, checksummed, monotonic.

sam: outline the motivation briefly?
mira: current opaque resume tokens tie to backend local state. anchors are emitted as part of stream payloads so the gateway has a transport-level hint to request resume from another worker without full replay. helps migration and reduces duplicate output.

raj: can you show the wire shape? keep it tiny.
mira: sketch: ANCHOR v1 := seq:u64 | bytes:u64 | token_hint:u32 | boundary:enum | crc32:hex. emitted periodically (every N tokens or on sentence boundary).

kevin: compatibility model: gateway treats anchors as optional. store latest anchor per request in-memory with a short TTL (default 30s) and fixed-size record. no disk writes.

lina: side-effects? if a webhook fired before anchor, resuming might repeat it. how do we reduce that risk?

mira: anchors don't solve idempotency. recommend backends optionally emit an idempotency_key when they perform external side-effects. gateway only attempts resume if backend advertises resume-capable and idempotency semantics acceptable for the route.

sam: partial anchor delivery risk? truncated frames could mislead gateway.

raj: compute CRC over canonicalized payload prefix and require full frame receipt. if CRC mismatch or truncated, gateway ignores anchor.

kevin: perf note: bound memory pressure by keeping only one anchor per stream and using TTL+LRU eviction. expose metrics: anchor_emitted, resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_fallback.

mira: rollout: wire proto + canonical CRC, gateway in-memory anchor store + TTL, backend resume API that accepts seq+crc, per-route rollout flag.

ops-bot: Mira posted RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/stream-anchors (auto-notify)

lina: +1 to a short sync with runtime/serving to prototype. default TTL 30s seems reasonable.
sam: +1

mira: will draft RFC checklist and ping runtime/serving for a 30-min prototype session.
